Further information: [List of European cities by population within city limits](/wiki/List_of_European_cities_by_population_within_city_limits "List of European cities by population within city limits")

The three largest [urban areas of Europe](/wiki/List_of_urban_areas_in_Europe "List of urban areas in Europe") are [Moscow](/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), [London](/wiki/London "London") and [Paris](/wiki/Paris "Paris"). All have over 10 million residents,[[314]](#cite_note-UN_WUP_2016-314) and as such have been described as [megacities](/wiki/Megacity "Megacity").[[315]](#cite_note-315) While [Istanbul](/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul") has the highest total city population, it lies partly in [Asia](/wiki/Asia "Asia"). 64.9% of the residents live on the European side and 35.1% on the Asian side.
The next largest cities in order of population are [Madrid](/wiki/Madrid "Madrid"), [Saint Petersburg](/wiki/Saint_Petersburg "Saint Petersburg"), [Milan](/wiki/Milan "Milan"), [Barcelona](/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"), [Berlin](/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"), and [Rome](/wiki/Rome "Rome") each having over three million residents.[[314]](#cite_note-UN_WUP_2016-314)

When considering the commuter belts or [metropolitan areas within Europe](/wiki/List_of_metropolitan_areas_in_Europe "List of metropolitan areas in Europe") (for which comparable data is available), Moscow covers the largest population, followed in order by Istanbul, London, Paris, Madrid, Milan, Ruhr Area, Saint Petersburg, Rhein-Süd, Barcelona and Berlin.[[316]](#cite_note-316)

White House intern [Monica Lewinsky](/wiki/Monica_Lewinsky "Monica Lewinsky") was also highly critical of the book, particularly the passages in which Clinton writes about [his affair with her](/wiki/Clinton%E2%80%93Lewinsky_scandal "Clinton–Lewinsky scandal"), saying that she had thought he would "correct the false statements he made when he was trying to protect the presidency."[[8]](#cite_note-USAT0625-8)

In the congressional elections of 1820, Buchanan ran for a seat in the [House of Representatives](/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives"). Shortly after his election victory, his father died in a carriage accident.[[17]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBaker200422-17) As a young Representative, Buchanan was one of the most prominent leaders of Pennsylvania's "Amalgamator party", which included both Democratic-Republicans and former Federalists. Buchanan's Federalist convictions declined, and he switched parties after opposing a nativist Federalist bill.[[18]](#cite_note-:0-18) During the [1824 presidential election](/wiki/1824_United_States_presidential_election "1824 United States presidential election"), Buchanan initially supported [Henry Clay](/wiki/Henry_Clay "Henry Clay") but switched to Andrew Jackson when it became clear that the Pennsylvanian public preferred Jackson.[[19]](#cite_note-19) After Jackson lost the 1824 election, he joined his faction.[[18]](#cite_note-:0-18)

In Washington, Buchanan became a defender of [states' rights](/wiki/States%27_rights "States' rights"), and was close with many southern Congressmen. Buchanan maintained strong ties to his constituency and helped build a Democratic coalition in Pennsylvania. In the 1828 presidential election, he supported Andrew Jackson and helped secure Pennsylvania.[[20]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBaker200424–27-20)

Buchanan gained attention during an impeachment trial in which he prosecuted federal district judge [James H. Peck](/wiki/James_H._Peck "James H. Peck"), whom the Senate acquitted. Yosemite has a [Mediterranean climate](/wiki/Mediterranean_climate "Mediterranean climate") ([Köppen climate classification](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") *Csa*), meaning most precipitation falls during the mild winter, and the other seasons are nearly dry (less than three percent of precipitation falls during the long, hot summers). Because of [orographic lift](/wiki/Orographic_lift "Orographic lift"), precipitation increases with elevation up to 8,000 feet (2,400 m) where it slowly decreases to the crest. Precipitation amounts vary from 36 inches (910 mm) at 4,000 feet (1,200 m) elevation to 50 inches (1,300 mm) at 8,600 feet (2,600 m). Snow does not typically accumulate until November in the high country. It deepens into March or early April.[[104]](#cite_note-climate-104)

Mean daily temperatures range from 25 °F (−4 °C) to 53 °F (12 °C) at Tuolumne Meadows at 8,600 feet (2,600 m). At the Wawona Entrance (elevation 5,130 feet or 1,560 metres), mean daily temperature ranges from 36 to 67 °F (2 to 19 °C). At the lower elevations below 5,000 feet (1,500 m), temperatures are hotter; the mean daily high temperature at Yosemite Valley (elevation 3,966 feet or 1,209 metres) varies from 46 to 90 °F (8 to 32 °C). At elevations above 8,000 feet (2,400 m), the hot, dry summer temperatures are moderated by frequent summer thunderstorms, along with snow that can persist into July. The combination of dry vegetation, low relative humidity, and thunderstorms results in frequent lightning-caused [fires](/wiki/Wildfire "Wildfire") as well.[[104]](#cite_note-climate-104)
